goals: Name gifts that believers describe as showing God sustains life.
notes: In this lesson, we explore what keeps people, plants and animals alive. Many families thank God for rain, sunshine and air. Rain helps crops grow; sunshine gives warmth and light; clean air helps us breathe.

activities: Observe the school garden. Name one way air, rainfall and sunlight help a living thing. Share what your family says about these gifts.
Draw a plant, a rain cloud and a bright sun. Show moving air with curved lines.

lessons.title: I Am Unique and Valuable
goals: Identify actions that build a healthy sense of identity and self-worth.
notes: Every child has qualities, interests and abilities. We grow in self-worth when we notice our strengths, practise a skill, speak kindly about ourselves and seek encouragement. Nobody needs to look or act exactly like another person to have value.
lessons.passage: Kwesi can tell stories, while Abena enjoys drawing. Their talents differ, yet both feel proud after sharing their work with classmates.
activities: In pairs, say one strength you have and one new skill you want to learn. Give your partner a kind, specific compliment.
Draw yourself doing something you enjoy. Write: “I can learn and improve.”

lessons.title: We Help in Our Families
goals: Identify different family roles and age-appropriate responsibilities.
notes: Families care for one another in many ways. Adults usually provide essentials such as food, shelter, safety and schooling. Children can contribute through safe, suitable chores, kindness and cooperation. Roles may be shared differently across families.

lessons.title: A Clean and Safe Environment
goals: Describe ways to keep surroundings clean and safe.
notes: Our surroundings include trees, soil, water, buildings and roads. Rubbish blocks drains and can harm people and animals. Putting waste in the right place, protecting water bodies, planting trees and following safety rules help our community.

lessons.title: Let Us Watch the Weather

notes: Weather describes outdoor conditions at a time. We can notice temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity and cloud cover. Symbols on a weather chart help us share observations across the week.

lessons.title: Important Crops Around Us

lessons.title: When Numbers of People Change

lessons.title: Respecting Ways of Worship
goals: Explain why worship matters to believers and how to respect different practices.
notes: In Ghana, Christians, Muslims and followers of African Traditional Religion may worship in different places and ways. Worship can express gratitude, devotion and commitment. Respect means allowing others to practise their faith peacefully without teasing or pressure.

lessons.title: Festivals Bring People Together

lessons.title: I Respect Ghana’s Symbols
goals: Explain ways to appreciate and protect national symbols.
notes: National symbols remind us that we belong to Ghana. They include the national flag, coat of arms and national anthem. Showing respect during the anthem, treating flags carefully and protecting public property are ways to show responsible citizenship.

Colour the three horizontal bands of the Ghana flag red, gold and green, with a black star in the middle.
lessons.safety: Use adult guidance for outdoor visits, tools and devices. Practise with safe classroom materials.

lessons.title: Ghana and Her Neighbours
goals: Name Ghana’s land neighbours and show their directions on a map.
notes: Ghana shares land borders with Côte d’Ivoire to the west, Burkina Faso to the north and Togo to the east. The Gulf of Guinea lies to Ghana’s south. Maps and cardinal directions help us locate places and learn about neighbouring countries.

Draw a labelled compass rose around a Ghana outline.

lessons.title: Where We Get Information
goals: Identify common sources from which people obtain information.
notes: Information can come from people, books, radios, telephones, newspapers, signs and other helpful sources. We listen, read, observe and ask questions. Since not every message is correct, children should check confusing claims with a trusted adult.

lessons.title: Sending and Receiving Messages
goals: Demonstrate safe ways of sending and receiving information.
notes: People share messages through talking, phone calls, SMS, posters, radio announcements and newspapers. A sender prepares information and a receiver gets it. Messages should be clear, useful and respectful. Children should not share private details with strangers.
lessons.passage: A school club makes a poster announcing a reading day. Parents receive the news through a school notice, and an adult sends a reminder message.
activities: Role-play a sender and receiver. Pass a short, safe message such as the time of a school event, then check whether it was understood.

sourceLesson.teacher_assessment:
Explore → Play → Challenge → Apply → Review. Each lesson has 5 Play and 10 non-identical Challenge multiple-choice prompts, physical/practical work, simple Ghanaian contexts and a lesson-specific illustration and local MP4. Use teacher observation for oral, kinaesthetic and creative performance in addition to quizzes.

The NaCCA early years programme is **integrated**, not four disconnected subjects. These four entry points deliberately share the seven prescribed themes. Preserve bilingual oral interactions and adapt examples to the child's home language and culture. Kindergarten learners need adult-guided play; don't force the multiple-choice quizzes as independent examinations.
